# @local/dsh-outbound-proxy

Host plugin for DeepSeek Harness that installs an outbound HTTP proxy policy in
the running Host pro

plugin for DeepSeek Harness that installs an outbound HTTP proxy policy in
the running Host process.
## Why

The Harness resolves its proxy policy once from the launch environment. A
desktop launch without `HT

TP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` leaves every Node-side
request (`web_fetch`, HTTP MCP transports, account

calls) connecting directly.
On a machine whose DNS answers come from a Clash-style fake-IP pool
(`19
8.18.0.0/15`), `web_fetch` refuses the request before it is sent:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What

The plugin calls `installProxyFromEnvironment` from
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-http-proxy` with the configure

d proxy URL. That replaces
undici's global dispatcher, which `web_fetch` consults through `proxyRout

P answer no longer matters. The installer also publishes the policy
through `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROX
Y`/`NO_PROXY` for child processes.

The module is imported from the Host's own runtime by file URL, so it is the
same instance `web_fetc

h` already uses — not a second, disconnected copy.
Candidates are derived from the launched script a

nd its ancestor directories
(the desktop Host passes the runtime root as `process.argv[2]`), then re

solved
through the runtime's own Node resolution. No installation path is hard-coded.

Loopback traffic always stays direct. Hosts in `noProxy` keep their direct route
(model provider, ac
count API), so stopping the proxy cannot strand a session.
## Configuration
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | Install the policy at all. Set `false` to leave routes untouched. |
| `proxyU
rl` | launch environment, else `http://127.0.0.1:7890` | Local HTTP(S) proxy URL; only `http://` / `

https://` are accepted. Leave it out to follow the device. |
| `noProxy` | `deepseek.com,opencode.ai
` | Comma-separated direct-connect suffixes. Loopback is always appended. |

Invalid explicit configuration fails activation with a message instead of
silently connecting direct

alid explicit configuration fails activation with a message instead of
silently connecting directly.
## Which port is used

The local mixed port differs per machine and per proxy client (Clash for
Windows defaults to `7890`,

Clash Verge to `7897`, others differ again), so the
plugin resolves the URL at mount time instead o

f baking one port into the
bundle:

1. `config.proxyUrl` in the row — an explicit per-device override, validated;
2. `https_proxy` / `HT

TPS_PROXY` / `http_proxy` / `HTTP_PROXY` from the launch
environment — on the desktop that is `%USER

http://127.0.0.1:7890` — the Clash for Windows default, only when neither
of the above names a proxy

ttp://127.0.0.1:7890` — the Clash for Windows default, only when neither
of the above names a proxy.
The Host console line states which one won:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

To set another port on a device, either put it in `~/.dsh/.env`
(`env/proxy.env` in this repository

is a template) or add `proxyUrl` to the
row — see INSTALL.md.
## Files

- `index.js` — Host plugin (`apply`, URL resolution, validation, module location).
- `cordis.patch.y

ml` — inserts the `outbound-proxy` row; leaves `proxyUrl` out so
each device follows its own environ

ment, and sets the direct-connect list
(`deepseek.com,opencode.ai`).
- `locale/{en,zh}.json` — displ

ay title/description.
- `icon.svg` — plugin icon.
- `INSTALL.md` — install/verify/uninstall notes.
